title: Why Oxygen Is Magnetic Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Liquid oxygen sticks to a magnet, liquid nitrogen runs straight past, and two helium atoms never stay together. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we learn molecular orbital theory, where atomic orbitals combine into orbitals of the whole molecule.

On the molecule bench, two 1s waves add to make the bonding orbital and cancel to make the antibonding orbital with a node, and electrons fill the energy levels of H2 and He2. We build bond order = 1/2 (Nb - Na) link by link, fill the 16 electrons of O2 to find bond order 2 and two unpaired electrons, and compare H2, He2, N2 and O2 with a magnet test. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question on O2 ions with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 49 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three puzzles: oxygen, nitrogen, helium
0:32 LCAO: orbitals of the whole molecule
1:05 The molecule bench: bonding and antibonding
1:51 Why He2 does not exist
2:04 Pause and think
2:17 Bond order, link by link
2:48 Worked example: why O2 is paramagnetic
3:25 H2, He2, N2 and O2 side by side
4:01 Exam trap: even electrons, still magnetic
4:25 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:00 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Hydrogen Bonding. Why does ice float on water, when most solids sink in their own liquid?
